title: Coping toolkit card and scenario
subject: PSHE
source: Written for pshe/y5 lesson 3 (Coping toolkit card and scenario (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 3: Looking after our minds and bodies. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Mind and body
points: Sleep, food and exercise help the mind

panels.title: Asking for help
points: If a feeling lasts or is very strong

passage.title: Bilal's week (a made-up scenario)
paras: Bilal is in Year 5. He has a spelling test tomorrow. His tummy feels tight and last night he could not sleep because he kept thinking about it. Today he did not want to play with his little brother after lessons, and he snapped at him.
Bilal has not told anyone how he feels. He thinks he is the only one who worries.

questions.q: What signs show that Bilal is worried? Name two.
questions.a: Any two: tight tummy (body); could not sleep; did not want to play; snapped at his brother.

questions.q: Write advice for Bilal: two coping strategies and who he could talk to.
questions.a: For example: slow breathing; make a short practice plan for the spellings; make du'a; talk to a parent or his teacher. Everyone worries sometimes.

keywords.def: a healthy way to deal with a hard feeling

questions.q: Match: worried about a test. One healthy strategy?
questions.a: Plan revision, breathe slowly, talk to a parent, make du'a.

questions.q: Do box breathing for one minute together.
Core: Make a personal 'toolkit' card of five coping strategies (pupil PDF).
Extend: Read the scenario and write advice for Bilal in the portal response box.
questions.a: Breathe, talk to his parent and teacher, sleep, make du'a.

questions.q: Stretch: Explain what resilience means with an example.
questions.a: Bouncing back: trying again after a poor mark.

questions.q: Which is a healthy coping strategy?
questions.a: B) Talking to a trusted adult. Sharing a worry with a trusted adult helps; the others make it worse.

questions.q: Mental health is about... A) how we think and feel B) only muscles C) only food
questions.a: A) how we think and feel

questions.q: Big question: what can you do when your mind feels worried?
questions.a: Breathe, talk to a trusted adult, move, make du'a.
